messages.content: My overtime on this week's payslip looks low. I did four 12-hour nights and a 6 on Friday. Why?

content.content:
payslip week Jan 10 to 16, 2028, paid Jan 21
provider gross paid $2197.40
provider overtime: 14 h x 1.5 x base $31.40
Hartwell rule recalculation:
HES-40217 week, TX, ruleset US-PAY v1.2
R-BASE  54 h x $31.40               $  1695.60
R-NIGHT 48 h x $2.75                $   132.00
R-BONUS weekly bonus                $   150.00
R-OT    14 h x 0.5 x $36.6222       $   256.36
gross                               $  2233.96
paid $36.56 less than the rule
payroll query PQ-28-0117 opened Jan 21 by the recalculation check; owner US payroll manager; any correction is paid by off-cycle payment

content.text:
Your payslip for January 10 to 16 shows 14 overtime hours, which matches your 54 hours (four 12-hour nights plus a 6-hour Friday). The gap is in how those hours were valued.

- Paid gross: $2197.40
- Hartwell rule recalculation: $2233.96
- Difference: $36.56 less than the rule

The rule values the 14 overtime hours at $256.36 (14 h x 0.5 x $36.6222). The provider line on the payslip uses 14 h x 1.5 x base $31.40. The system flagged the mismatch and opened payroll query PQ-28-0117, which the US payroll manager owns. Any correction would be paid as an off-cycle payment.

I can't change your pay. Do you want me to send this to the payroll team with the query details?

R-BASE  54 h x $31.40               $  1695.60

- Weekly bonus: $150.00
- Overtime: 20 h x 0.5 x $36.1000 = $361.00
- Gross: $2527.00

This is an estimate only. The final figure comes from payroll.

content.content: request PIR-NL-28-014 logged for HW-NL0101; received March 6, 2028; written answer due by May 6, 2028; answered by Hartwell Netherlands HR (reward) in writing; the agent holds no other person's pay

content.text:
I can't give you average pay figures for other workers, including men in your job category. I've logged your request as PIR-NL-28-014 under pay transparency law.
